old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a single snowflake against a gradient background transitioning from yellow at the top to blue at the bottom. The snowflake is centrally positioned and exhibits intricate hexagonal patterns with multiple arms extending outward. Each arm is detailed with smaller facets, giving it a three-dimensional appearance. The lighting highlights the snowflake's edges, creating a glowing effect that emphasizes its delicate structure. Throughout the video, there are no significant changes or movements; the focus remains solely on the snowflake, allowing viewers to appreciate its complex and symmetrical design. The consistent framing and lack of additional elements ensure that the viewer's attention is drawn entirely to the beauty and intricacy of the snowflake.

caption: The video showcases a six-armed, snowflake-like crystal at the center of the frame, built from faceted, translucent blue prisms trimmed with bright yellow edges around a small star at the core. The backdrop is a smooth vertical gradient from warm yellow at the top to pale blue at the bottom, unchanged throughout. Across the excerpt the crystal steadily enlarges, its six outward-pointing arms stretching longer and increasing the structure's overall span. The central star and the six-fold arrangement keep a fixed position and orientation, so the change reads as pure expansion of the arms rather than rotation or sideways drift. The blue and yellow color scheme remains constant under steady lighting, and the enlargement proceeds from the first view to the last.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
